title: Predicate for rational and common-stage Weil duality with coefficient diagrams
statement: Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and a separated finite-type model $X_0$. Use the actual common-stage duality and its finite rational data, internal-Hom identification and exceptional-unit dualizing normalization of [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data], the derived coefficient operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], Weil pairs of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and constructible exceptional adjunctions of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Define the predicate Conclusion as follows. There exist such duality data $B_X$, an identification with the recorded internal Hom, the specified exceptional-unit dualizing normalization, and finite/common Weil structures $W_X$. Their dual comparison uses $D(\theta^{-1})$; evaluation and actual biduality obey the Weil equations. The canonical dualizing and dual scalar comparisons for every finite field inclusion, including identity inclusions, and the finite-to-common inclusion comparisons obey the corresponding Weil equations, with their prescribed evaluation/biduality diagrams. The dualizing Weil structure is normalized by the mate of the actual structure-morphism exchange and the unit-normalized constant object. For every separated finite-type $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ between separated finite-type models and every model compactification there exist corresponding $B_Y$, an actual exceptional functor on its geometric compactification, its internal-Hom/dualizing identifications and exceptional-duality formula, and $W_Y$, with that same dualizing normalization. The exceptional Frobenius comparison is the mate of inverse compact-support exchange; the actual units, counits, finite scalar and common-stage adjunction comparisons have their prescribed Weil equations. This paragraph defines a proposition packaging all these witnesses and diagrams; it does not assert that the proposition holds.
